newsitem.title: USA: Northeast Utils units raise auditor doubts.
newsitem.headline: Northeast Utils units raise auditor doubts.

text.p: Northeast Utilities said on Monday that its financial statements for two subsidiaries contain paragraphs by its auditors that note "substantial doubt" about their ability to continue as going concerns.

Arthur Andersen LLP said uncertainties around Public Service Co of New Hampshire and North Atlantic Energy Corp prompted the statement, since the New Hampshire Public Utilities Commission ordered a restructuring of the electric power business.

Northeast Utilities said the New Hampshire order could lead to $400 million in writeoffs and would result in defaults that would give investors and lenders the right to accelerate payment on $1.2 billion of debt owed by the two subsidiaries.
Northeast also said it has lined up financing that is expected to be adequate to fund the return of its Millstone nuclear power plant into service.
The company said, however, that any delays would require additional funding or cost cutting.

Northeast Utilities said it is currently maintaining access to a new $313 million credit agreement that expires March 28, but the company expects it to be extended until November 1999, pending approval of certain amendments.

Northeast Utilities said it continues to maintain access to $240 million through the sale of receivables, $225 million through a revolving credit agreement for Public Service New Hampshire and $56 million under separate banklaon agreements for its operations outside New Hampshire.
In 1996, Northeast expensed $403 million on Millstone-related non-fuel operation and maintenance costs in 1996, including $179 million related to outages.
Northeast said it expects to expanse $386 million in Millstone-related costs in 1997.
Millstone is expected to have at least one of the units on line by the end of 1997, the company said.
